Male to Male Fittings - This is a slick product. We've had trouble with the hose sliding off the vent pipe, so this is a great idea. A couple warnings though:
1) The plastic connectors are both male fittings. If the pipe in your wall is also a male fitting, the plastic coupler will not slide into it, even after you prepared it as in the instructions. And once you've cut it as instructed, it is compromised--and inside the wall. I straightened out the tabs I cut in the pipe and used aluminum duct tape to attach the platic fitting to the pipe in the wall. I'm hoping the adhesive on the tape will hold up under the heat. Otherwise I will need to cut a larger hole in the wall to replace the elbow that I damaged preparing it for the DryerDock fitting.
2) You rotate the two pieces together to attach. There's not a lot of friction holding them in place (they don't truely "lock"). If there's much spring force to twist them back counter-clockwise, they will come apart. I'm planning to drill a hole through the two to insert a pin & thus lock them in place.

Docking (no pun intended) one star because the instructions could have warned about pipe fitting incompatibilities & the locking mechanism could be better.

All that being said, I'm planning on buying a second DryerDock to put on the dryer side of the hose, as the hose tends to slide off there too. The dryer side connector also looks to be male, so I'm going to check at a hardware store for a short slip fitting to join the two male ends.

Better than original Whynter cord! - The original cord was shorter than the AC cord. This made it a bit less convenient to find places to put it in the car. So when I had to replace the original cord (It had the tip of the plug broken off) I looked for a replacement. I saw this, and while rather expensive I decided to order it. The new cord is a heavier gauge wire than the original, which is a good safety feature that keeps the wire from overheating and also wastes less of our battery from resistance. It is MUCH easier to find a good place to put the cooler when you have ten feet of cord! The only small minus is that unlike the old cord that has a straight plug, this has a 90 degree right angle. So even if the 12v port is on the left you still have it going off to the right before you bend it over. On a short cord this would make it harder to reach the port if it's on the wrong side. But with this much length it just looks a bit funny...

So, while I wish it wasn't so expensive I think it's worth it. I wish Whynter had an option of buying the cooler with it instead of the short cord!

For your new refrigerator - Over time your refrigerators filter housing can fall victim to high mineral content of your local water supply. Installing this system can protect your overly expensive refrigerator internal components by never allowing it to enter it's system. I wish that I'd done this when our Samsung refrigerator was still new. Over time the filter housing just began to deliver a weak stream of water to the door. Typical cost to replace the housing with labor is around $500 or so. If your system is working fine at the moment I highly recommend an external filter like this one. It's solved our issue for a few bucks and 30 minutes of my time. It came with a lot of extra water line so flushing the filter into the kitchen sink before attaching it to the refrigerator was easy. Say goodbye to that low volume and expensive factory filter that you have to replace twice a year (my frig fitler was on a timer and not a flow meter every six months) and say hello to a uncontaminated refrigerator water supply system, less expensive high quality filters, and less maintenance.

Side of the device "melted" and the fan shakes so hard the unit turns off. - We were super excited about getting the new ice machine and things were going great, until they weren't.

Received the ice maker approximately 28 Nov 21 - Did not plug it in and put it into service until approximately 24 Jan 22. Hey, we have some neurodivergence in the house so it took a little bit to get there. This ultimately was the "downfall" for being able to return this product as the return time ran out on 31 Jan 22.

The good: This thing pumps out ice at the rate the manual and listing states. It has some cute cubes and they are small enough to fit most of the reusable bottles/cups we use here in the home.

The not so good: After 31-days of use the fan (located on the back right side of the unit) seems to be loose or broken and now, at least once a day will rattle so loud and hard that the unit shuts down. There is, what appears to be, a spot where the unit overheated and "melted" the side, to the tune of an approximate area of 6" x 4" as notated by the picture with the ruler. The unit began to "auto shut off" about 2-weeks into use, but it was not consistent and we could not figure out why, shortly after is when we noticed the melted section. So it seems there may be a defect (possibly just with the one we purchased) in this one.

Maybe this unit does not support being plugged in 24hrs a day? I may have missed that in the instructions. However, for a $129 unit to last 31 days, just long enough to get past the return point, that also does not seem right. We plan to find a new countertop ice maker, likely from a different company, we expected more from a Frigidaire product.

We do hope you have great success with your item if you choose to purchase this product.
